item.title: Trump threatens Oman, Iran war in stalemate as 60-day talks window ends
item.description: The 60-day deadline for the U.S. and Iran to negotiate a peace deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz is expiring, with no agreement in sight.

item.title: Blanche refuses to say Justice Department will always act independently from Trump
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche weighed in on questions about the Justice Department acting independently from the White House. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman reports.

item.title: Watch Live: Lindsay Clancy murder trial resumes, prosecution may rest today
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's Massachusetts murder trial is back underway Monday in Plymouth Superior Court with a fourth week of witness testimony.

item.title: New poll shows majority of Americans feel way the U.S. economic system works is unfair
item.description: A recent CBS News poll provides further insight into views of the U.S. economy and voters' views on the popularity of socialism. Anthony Salvanto has more.

item.title: BBC asks court to subpoena Trump family members for defamation defense
item.description: After failing to deliver subpoenas itself, the BBC has asked a Florida court to compel three of President Trump's family members to testify over the Jan. 6 attack on the Capitol.

item.title: CENTCOM commander meets with troops on USS Abraham Lincoln as critics slam conditions
item.description: Adm. Brad Cooper, the head of U.S. Central Command, met with troops aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln as concerns linger about morale and apparent worsening conditions. CBS News analyst Aaron MacLean has more insight.

item.title: Novak Djokovic says health condition has been bothering him for "past couple of years"
item.description: Tennis star Novak Djokovic lost in the second round of the Cincinnati Open over the weekend and appeared to struggle with stamina throughout the match. On Saturday, he attributed his on-court issues to a health condition that has been bothering him "for the past couple of years" and said it's exacerbated by hot and humid conditions.

item.title: Growing backlash amid privacy concerns over Flock cameras
item.description: There's rising scrutiny over Flock Safety's nationwide network of cameras that record license plate numbers. Over the weekend, a protest turned physical in Fargo, North Dakota, while officials in Hood County, Texas, shut down and covered its cameras over privacy concerns. Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere dies at 36
item.description: Actress Hayden Panettiere, known for her roles in "Remember the Titans" and "Heroes," has died at 36, her publicist confirmed. CBS News' Bradley Blackburn reports.

item.title: Trump family's World Liberty Financial granted bank status
item.description: A Trump-appointed bank regulator has given conditional approval for World Liberty Financial, a crypto business established by President Trump's sons and the sons of special envoy Steve Witkoff, to become a bank. Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Questions over when USS Lincoln will return following concerns about ship conditions
item.description: The head of U.S. Central Command visited the USS Lincoln over the weekend amid questions over when the ship will return from the Middle East. Families of sailors and members of Congress raised concerns over conditions on the ship during its nine-month deployment. Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Former Hurricane Lala drenches Hawaii, flash floods sweep away Big Island homes
item.description: Lala was weakening but still packing a punch as it moved away from the islands, forecasters said.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere, known for "Heroes" and "Remember the Titans," dies at 36
item.description: Hayden Panettiere, who starred in "Remember the Titans" as a child actor and rose to fame in the sci-fi series "Heroes," has died at the age of 36.

item.title: Aerial video shows extensive damage after Hurricane Lala slammed Hawaii
item.description: The cleanup is beginning in Hawaii after it was hit by Hurricane Lala, which has now weakened to a tropical storm. Floodwaters washed out roads, and thousands of people are without power. Jonathan Vigliotti reports.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere, known for roles in "Nashville" and "Heroes," dies at 36
item.description: Actor Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36, her father confirmed in a statement. The star was known for her roles in "Heroes" and "Nashville." Gayle King has a look at her life and career.

item.title: Eye Opener: Tributes pour in for Hayden Panettiere after actor's shocking death at 36
item.description: Hayden Panettiere is remembered by fans and Hollywood following the actor's shocking death at 36 years old. Plus, a look at the damage left behind by Hurricane Lala after it slammed Hawaii with strong winds and torrential rain. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: Woman fights off bear with spray after being attacked on trail in Alaska
item.description: A woman was running alone on a path called the Wolverine Bowl Trail when the brown bear attacked her, officials said.

item.title: Thousands waiting for help as Indonesia earthquake death toll nears 70
item.description: Thousands of people are still waiting for aid on Indonesia's Flores island days after a powerful earthquake killed at least 68 people.

item.title: Trial starting after Microsoft exec's alleged murder-for-hire involving ex-wife
item.description: Jared Bridegan was repeatedly shot outside his vehicle while his 2-year-old child was strapped in a car seat.

item.title: U.K. prime minister messages with impersonator of top Trump staffer
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham exchanged messaged with someone pretending to be White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.

item.title: Trump orders Pentagon to "substantially reduce" military exercises with South Korea
item.description: President Trump said Sunday that the joint military exercises with South Korea are costly and they "send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile" to North Korea.

item.title: CENTCOM chief visits USS Abraham Lincoln amid morale concerns
item.description: Meanwhile, Israel is being condemned by Lebanese leaders for strikes in the south that killed at least 11 people, including children.

item.title: U.S. tourist reportedly killed by lightning strike on Italy's Mount Etna
item.description: An American man hiking up Italy's active Mount Etna volcano was killed by a lightning strike, the national news agency ANSA reports.

item.title: RFK Jr.'s hunt for autism culprits stalls amid Trump's baseless vaccine order
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s closed-door research has yet to produce evidence linking vaccines and autism.

item.title: Jared Kushner met with Hamas leaders in Egypt to discuss Gaza peace deal
item.description: Jared Kushner, who is President Trump's son-in-law, is set to meet next with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who rejected the latest peace proposal last week.

item.title: Beshear says he's "heard absolutely nothing" from McConnell
item.description: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear said he hasn't heard back from Sen. Mitch McConnell following formal requests for an update on his health last month amid a weekslong hospitalization.

item.title: Rahm Emanuel on Trump, the left, and what's right for America
item.description: As a Democratic Congressman, Chicago mayor, ambassador, and chief of staff in the Obama White House, Rahm Emanuel has been a key and combative moderate; he says his fight, now and in the future, is bigger than him and his party.

item.title: A summer of extremes: Weathering a hotter world
item.description: July was the hottest month ever in the Lower 48 States – another escalation of our world into a hotter, more dangerous planet, where extreme weather events – such as heat waves, wildfires and hurricanes – will become more common and more extreme.

item.title: Air traffic controller saves day when 2 jets with same call number converge
item.description: An air traffic controller's quick thinking helped avert a dangerous situation when two jets, one landing in Phoenix and the other simultaneously taking off, shared the same flight number and radio frequency.

item.title: Construction workers find $10 million gold stash in renovations
item.description: Police issued a warning telling "gold prospectors" to stay away from the construction site
